To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) patients with all clinic diastolic pressures > 90 mm Hg had a high blood load in 65% of cases; 2) patients with at least one clinic reading of < 100 mm Hg had high blood load in only 35% of cases; and 3) the difference between these two groups was statistically significant.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the diagnosis of hypertension and the role of clinic blood pressure in its assessment.
the relationship between clinic blood pressure and 24 hour ambulatoy blood pressure monitoring in the diagnosis of essential hypertension.
the relationship between clinic blood pressure and 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure in the diagnosis of high blood pressure in patients with hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the diagnosis of hypertension is best established with the use of ambulatory blood pressure recording.
a single elevated clinic blood pressure is not a good indicator of hypertension, but a consistently elevated clinic blood pressure may be a better predictor of hypertension.
the presence of consistently raised diastolics is a better predictor of hypertension than a single low diastolic reading.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of clinic diastolic pressure alone is not a good predictor of blood pressure status defined as blood pressure load.
clinic diastolic pressure readings have limited predictive power as to blood pressure status defined as blood pressure load.
clinic blood pressure readings are not good predictors of blood pressures status.
The main takeaway from our work is that
clinic blood pressure measurements are not good enough to diagnose hypertension.
blood pressure load, as assessed by 24 hour ambulatoy monitoring, is more predictive of true hypertension than are clinic blood pressure readings.
the blood pressure load is a better indicator of the true status of the patient than a simple clinic reading.
